title: FloodSentry
problem_statement: Water damage is the second most common home insurance claim in the US, averaging $11,098 per incident, and 93% of events are preventable if detected within the first hour. Vacation and investment rental property owners—numbering 6.5 million in the US—face disproportionate risk because their properties sit unoccupied for 2+ weeks at a time, averaging 19 hours of undetected water intrusion per event. Existing smart leak detectors from Moen Flo and Phyn rely exclusively on Wi-Fi and fail silently during storms that simultaneously knock out internet service and burst pipes. A cellular-backup water leak sensor with 72-hour battery life and SMS alerting independent of home Wi-Fi closes this critical coverage gap.
target_users: Vacation property owner who visits their second home fewer than 26 times per year and has no on-site caretaker
Short-term rental (STR) host managing one or more investment properties remotely via platforms like Airbnb or VRBO
Long-distance landlord overseeing residential rental units in a different city or state without a local property manager
Property management company managing 10+ residential or vacation units on behalf of absentee owners
High-value primary homeowner with finished basement or luxury fixtures seeking insurance premium reduction
user_stories: As a vacation property owner who visits their second home fewer than 26 times per year and has no on-site caretaker, I want to receive an SMS alert within 5 minutes of water detection even when the cabin's internet router is offline so that I can dispatch a local plumber before a burst fitting escalates to mold remediation.

As a vacation property owner who visits their second home fewer than 26 times per year and has no on-site caretaker, I want the sensor to operate for at least 72 hours on battery alone so that a power outage during a storm does not create a silent failure window while I am unreachable.

As a short-term rental (STR) host managing one or more investment properties remotely via platforms like Airbnb or VRBO, I want to configure multiple alert recipients including my co-host and local handyman so that water events are actioned even when I am in a different time zone or unavailable.

As a short-term rental (STR) host managing one or more investment properties remotely via platforms like Airbnb or VRBO, I want to view a dashboard showing the real-time status and last-check-in timestamp of all my sensors across multiple properties so that I can confirm coverage before and during guest stays.

As a long-distance landlord overseeing residential rental units in a different city or state without a local property manager, I want to receive a low-battery warning at least 7 days before battery depletion so that I can arrange for the tenant or a contractor to replace batteries before a coverage gap occurs.

As a property management company managing 10+ residential or vacation units on behalf of absentee owners, I want to access a multi-property management portal with role-based permissions and exportable incident logs so that I can provide documented proof of monitoring diligence to property owners and insurers.

As a high-value primary homeowner with finished basement or luxury fixtures seeking insurance premium reduction, I want to receive an automatically generated monitoring activity report monthly so that I can submit it to my insurance carrier as evidence of continuous leak detection for potential premium discounts.
acceptance_criteria: Sensor detects standing water contact and transmits an alert via cellular within 5 minutes under conditions where Wi-Fi is completely unavailable, verified in controlled lab testing with router powered off.

Sensor operates continuously on internal battery for a minimum of 72 hours with cellular connectivity active and no AC power, confirmed by continuous uptime logging in a temperature-controlled environment at 68°F.
SMS alert is delivered to all configured recipient phone numbers within 5 minutes of water detection in 99% of test trials across three US cellular carriers (AT&T, T-Mobile, Verizon).
Sensor transmits a cellular health heartbeat signal at least once every 60 minutes; failure to receive two consecutive heartbeats triggers a 'sensor offline' SMS notification to the account owner.

Low-battery alert is sent via SMS and displayed in the app dashboard when battery capacity drops to 20% or less, which must correspond to at least 7 days of remaining operational life under standard usage.
Mobile app and web dashboard display real-time sensor status (online, offline, alerting, battery level, last check-in timestamp) with data refreshed at least every 5 minutes.

Multi-property portal allows a property management company account to add up to 100 sensor devices across unlimited properties and assign role-based access (admin, viewer, responder) with no degradation in alert latency.
Device enclosure achieves IP67 rating for dust and water ingress, verified by third-party testing per IEC 60529 standard.
Sensor installation requires no tools and is completable by a non-technical user in under 10 minutes, validated by usability testing with 10 participants achieving task completion without assistance.

Monthly monitoring activity report is automatically generated as a PDF on the first calendar day of each month, includes per-sensor uptime percentage, alert history, and battery log, and is emailed to the account holder.

success_metrics.metric: Mean time from water detection to SMS delivery (cellular path)
success_metrics.baseline: No existing cellular-backup product benchmark; Wi-Fi-only competitors average 2-3 minutes under ideal conditions
success_metrics.target: ≤5 minutes in 99% of events measured across production devices in the first 6 months post-launch

success_metrics.metric: 30-day sensor uptime rate (device reachable via cellular or Wi-Fi heartbeat)
success_metrics.target: ≥98% average uptime across all active deployed devices within 3 months of general availability

success_metrics.metric: Monthly active devices (MAD) — sensors that have transmitted at least one heartbeat in the trailing 30 days
success_metrics.target: 10,000 active devices by end of month 12 post-launch

success_metrics.metric: Net Promoter Score (NPS) among activated device owners surveyed at 90 days post-purchase
success_metrics.baseline: Industry average for smart home hardware: 32 (Qualtrics 2023)
success_metrics.target: NPS ≥50 by end of Q2 post-launch, based on minimum 500 survey responses

success_metrics.metric: False positive alert rate (water alert triggered without actual water present)
success_metrics.baseline: Moen Flo reported false positive complaints in ~8% of user reviews on Amazon (internal analysis)
success_metrics.target: False positive rate ≤2% of total alerts generated across the fleet in any rolling 30-day window

success_metrics.metric: Average revenue per device per year (hardware + cellular subscription)
success_metrics.target: $65 blended ARPU per device per year (hardware amortized over 3 years at $89 MSRP + $24/year cellular plan) by month 18

risks_open_questions: Cellular carrier coverage: What percentage of US vacation and rural rental properties fall outside reliable LTE/CAT-M1 coverage, and does FloodSentry need a satellite fallback tier for extremely remote cabins?

Regulatory and carrier certification: FCC Part 15/Part 22 certification and carrier IoT SIM approval timelines could extend hardware launch by 3-6 months; how does this affect the go-to-market schedule?

Battery chemistry trade-off: Achieving 72-hour battery life with cellular radio active requires careful selection between lithium primary cells (non-rechargeable, lower cost) and LiPo rechargeable packs; which strategy optimizes total cost of ownership for multi-year deployment?

Cellular plan unit economics: IoT SIM costs from carriers range from $1-$5/month per device; at scale, does a managed MVNO relationship or a direct carrier agreement become necessary to preserve margin on the $24/year plan price?

Insurance carrier partnerships: What documentation format and data standards do major home insurers (State Farm, Allstate, USAA) require to validate monitoring activity for premium discount programs, and can we meet those standards at launch?

Silent failure detection completeness: If the cellular modem itself fails (hardware fault), the heartbeat mechanism also fails; what secondary watchdog mechanism ensures the homeowner is notified of a non-communicating sensor?

Sensor placement guidance: Optimal placement (under sinks, near water heaters, at washing machine hoses) is non-obvious; inadequate placement guidance risks false negatives and customer churn — how prescriptive should in-box instructions and the app onboarding flow be?

Channel strategy for property management companies: PMCs require volume pricing, API integrations with property management software (Buildium, AppFolio), and dedicated account support; is this B2B segment addressable at launch or deferred to phase 2?

Regulatory compliance for SMS alerting: TCPA requires express written consent for automated SMS in certain contexts; how does consent collection integrate into device activation without creating friction that reduces opt-in rates?

Competitive response risk: Moen Flo and Phyn have significant distribution and brand recognition; what is the likelihood they add cellular backup within 12-18 months of FloodSentry's launch, and how does the roadmap sustain differentiation?
out_of_scope: Automatic water shutoff valve integration or motorized valve control in version 1.0
Water quality or contamination monitoring (e.g., lead, pH, hardness detection)
Wi-Fi-only operation mode as a cost-reduced SKU in the initial product line
Integration with smart home platforms (Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Apple HomeKit, SmartThings) prior to version 2.0
International markets outside the contiguous United States, Alaska, and Hawaii at launch
Flood or groundwater intrusion detection (exterior perimeter, sump pit overflow) — focus is indoor plumbing leak detection only in v1
Homeowner's insurance claims filing automation or direct insurer API integration at launch
Video or image capture at the sensor location to visually confirm water presence
Proprietary cellular network infrastructure — FloodSentry will use existing third-party CAT-M1/NB-IoT carrier networks exclusively
Consumer mobile app features beyond sensor status monitoring and alert management, such as home maintenance scheduling or contractor marketplace
